rationale: The agent saw that the split was by pair, not by protein: 59 of 60 proteins appear in both train and test, which roughly matches the key's ~100% overlap. It also said per-protein propensity features would overstate performance on unseen proteins, so it left protein identity out and presented its co-expression-only AUROC of 0.65 as the held-out result. It never proposed a protein-disjoint split or a breakdown by how many of a pair's proteins were seen in training, and it didn't run the propensity baseline.
